title: Stabilize TOML diagnostics across the declared supported Bun runtime range
summary: Stabilize TOML diagnostics across the declared supported Bun runtime range
description:
Reported from the cli-test review and Orbitfall project exercise on 2026-09-04. Installed tools: Lore 0.4.1 and Quest 0.3.2, macOS ARM64. Source review revisions: Lore 054e6590f1b81fda418c9891611f84fd35aacf6e; Quest dcb06f6520e08f2755c04166cca168318a94ae5a. Findings describe those tested versions, not a claim that current HEAD was retested. Evidence paths below are retained in the sibling cli-test checkout; the reproduction and outcomes are also included here. Filing is not a fix.

Source/runtime compatibility finding, distinct from the installed native binary: package engines advertises bun >=1.3.14, with packageManager pinned to 1.3.14. In disposable clones of the recorded Lore revision, run bun test test/config.test.ts with Bun 1.3.14 and Bun 1.4.0.
Observed: all 47 configuration tests pass on 1.3.14; five fail on 1.4.0. Full suites: pinned 2809 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail; 1.4.0 2804 pass / 1 skip / 5 fail. The failures concern malformed TOML reason classes, parser submessages and unsafe integer hints/signs, including parent_page_id = 9007199254740993 under [confluence]. src/config.ts relies on native Bun.TOML.parse diagnostic wording.
Expected: actionable stable Lore diagnostics across the supported range, or an accurately constrained/documented runtime support contract. This is not evidence that the compiled installed binary fails on those inputs.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Malformed TOML and unsafe positive/negative integer diagnostics expose stable actionable Lore errors on every advertised supported runtime.
The five failing configuration contracts pass, or intentionally revised contracts and support bounds are documented with justification.
CI covers the pinned runtime and the newest supported runtime so parser wording changes are detected.

implementationNotes:
Reproduced exactly as filed: bun test test/config.test.ts passes 50/50 on Bun 1.3.14 (this project's pinned floor), fails 5 on Bun 1.4.2 (the newest available release at the time -- close enough to the filed 1.4.0 to confirm the same class of drift; not re-tested against 1.4.0 exactly since 1.4.2 is what bun upgrade installs today and reproduces the identical five failures the filing described).

Root cause, verified directly rather than assumed: two independent behavior changes in Bun's native Bun.TOML.parse between 1.3.14 and 1.4.x.
(1) Malformed-TOML error wording changed entirely -- 1.3.14 throws with an "Unexpected ..." style message (sometimes as an AggregateError whose sub-messages get flattened by config.ts's describeCause), 1.4.x throws a single differently-worded "TOML Parse error: ..." message. Lore's OWN contract (prefix the parser's reason with ".lore/config.toml is not valid TOML: ", never leak Bun's internal BuildMessage class name) was already correct and unaffected on both versions -- only two tests over-specified Bun's exact wording as if it were part of lore's own contract.
(2) An imprecise bare unquoted integer literal (parent_page_id = 9007199254740993, and its negative form) is handled differently: 1.3.14 silently rounds it to the nearest representable double and lore's own asPageId Number.isSafeInteger check catches the rounded value, producing lore's specific "quote it to preserve precision" hint; 1.4.x's parser now REJECTS the literal at parse time, before lore's own validation ever runs, with Bun's own precision message instead. This is a genuine, verified upstream behavior change, not a lore defect -- both outcomes are stable, actionable validation errors, just produced by different layers depending on the runtime.

Decision (AC2's "intentionally revised contracts... documented with justification"): keep asPageId's too-large-number branch as-is (still correct and reachable on 1.3.14, lore's pinned floor; harmless dead code on runtimes where Bun's own parser intercepts it first) and document the cross-runtime split directly in its own doc comment. Update the five affected tests to accept EITHER observed shape (Bun's own parse-time rejection, or lore's own asPageId diagnostic) rather than assuming one specific runtime's behavior, so they stay green across the whole declared-supported range without weakening what each actually verifies: lore's own stable prefix/no-class-name-leak contract for the malformed-TOML cases, and "some actionable validation error naming the config file" for the integer-precision cases. One conformance-table entry ("imprecise numeric page id retains the quote-it diagnostic") was removed from the byte-compatible REJECTED_CONFIG_CONFORMANCE_V1 table, since its exact expected shape is no longer byte-stable across runtimes by definition -- its coverage moved to the dedicated version-tolerant test instead, with a comment explaining why it isn't in the table.

AC3: added a new CI job, config-test-newest-bun -- narrow and fast (bun test test/config.test.ts only, not the full suite) against Bun "latest" via oven-sh/setup-bun, rather than doubling the whole matrix's cost for a risk specifically scoped to Bun.TOML.parse wording. Verified locally first that bun install --frozen-lockfile --linker=isolated succeeds under 1.4.2 against this repo's own committed lockfile (no lockfile-shape incompatibility), matching the release-runbook's documented trap before trusting the CI job to work at all. Given the standard exactHostSkipGuard if: condition like every other unrelated job (verified via test/ci-workflow.test.ts's own exhaustive job-contract test, updated).

Verified: full suite (2884 tests) green on BOTH Bun 1.3.14 and Bun 1.4.2, not just test/config.test.ts in isolation -- confirms no OTHER hidden Bun-version-sensitive failures exist beyond the five found. typecheck clean; lint exit 0 (one pre-existing unrelated warning); lore check 77 files, 0 errors.
